flowable.database: PostgreSQL (Testcontainers postgres:17-alpine, server 17.11, fresh database per engine instance)
flowable.historyLevel: AUDIT (Flowable default; the adapter does not set it)
engineConfigurationAsUsed: adapter as installed: async executor off (timers via executeDueJobs), DMN and CMMN configurators, history level not set by the adapter (engine default)
the engine clock is per engine configuration (shared by the DMN/CMMN engines)
flowable.threads: GP-08: 4 worker threads for start and for completion on both engines; GP-09: 1 thread (completions of one multi-instance body conflict by design on both engines)

scenarios.title: Maker -> checker -> approver by seat, with amount bands (DMN FIRST)
featuresUsed: userTask candidate group by seat: potentialOwner group(${seat})
DMN 1.3 decision table, hit policy FIRST, called from BPMN
variants: DMN call: serviceTask flowable:type=dmn + field decisionTableReferenceKey (outputs become process variables)
notes: Neither engine enforces segregation of duties (maker != checker != approver): the same user claimed both tasks. SoD by person and by seat is a product-layer check (R19 / A-3, IX.5 item 5).

scenarios.title: Multi-level hierarchy with return to any earlier level (e-Office noting)
featuresUsed: exclusive gateway router (one gateway, conditions on ${next})
notes: Return to any level is modelled (router gateway); the native instance-modification API was also checked as an alternative for out-of-model returns.

scenarios.title: Committee: all members must sign
Committee quorum (n of m)
Chained sanctions AA -> TS -> ES (call activities)
featuresUsed: variables in/out of the called process
candidate group by seat inside the called process
variants: flowable:in sourceExpression / flowable:out source on callActivity (BPMN 2.0.2 has no executable call-activity variable mapping)

scenarios.title: SLA with working-day calendar, holidays, reminders, escalation
featuresUsed: boundary timer non-interrupting timeDate ${slaDue} (due date computed by the product calendar)
boundary timer non-interrupting timeDuration P3D on a working-day business calendar
variants: flowable:businessCalendarName="govWorkingDays" on the P3D timer (named calendar per timer)
notes: Portable form: the product layer computes the due date with its holiday calendar and the model uses timeDate ${slaDue} (no variant). Engine-calendar form: Flowable selects a named calendar per timer; Operaton can only replace the engine-wide calendar of a timer type.

scenarios.title: Deadline extension of running instances (tender corrigendum)
featuresUsed: timer job due-date change on running instances
notes: rescheduleTimeDateJob deletes the timer job and creates a new one (new job id)
Model-based alternative without native API: event-based gateway with a 'corrigendum' message that loops back to the timer with the new date (used in D-TENDER, E17-a).

scenarios.title: Bulk intake: >= 5,000 instances, bulk approve / reject / withdraw
featuresUsed: task queries by seat and by process variable

workarounds.what: bulk approve/reject: neither engine has a bulk task-completion API; the product layer pages task ids and completes them with 4 threads

scenarios.title: Large multi-instance (>= 5,000 items in one instance)
featuresUsed: history volume of one large instance
failures: all 5000 items completed within the cap of 180000 ms (completed 1290 in 180170 ms; per-completion cost grows with the number of open items)
notes: Not finished within the cap: completing one item of a parallel multi-instance body costs time proportional to the open items (total ~ n^2). Workaround for beneficiary lists: one instance per item (GP-08 shape, linear) or chunked sub-processes; not measured here.

scenarios.title: Multi-year process with monthly cycles (36 monthly bills)
notes: Runtime rows of the running instance grow with every cycle ({ACT_RU_ACTINST=175}): a multi-year instance carries its activity trail in runtime tables until it ends
BPMN has no continue-as-new; the instance stays one instance for 3 years and history grows per cycle.
P1M repeats from the previous due date, so a cycle started on the 31st drifts to the 28th after February; a fixed billing day needs a cron-like cycle or a date computed by the product

scenarios.title: Budget availability + encumbrance (idempotent), released on cancel by compensation

workarounds.what: no working compensation with a wait-state handler: cancel boundary -> explicit release external task -> cancelled (no compensation event)

productLayer.what: encumbrance ledger and its idempotency check (operationId) live in the product layer

notes: Compensation with a wait-state handler (external task) failed on this engine; the cancel is rolled back. Fallback: the cancel path is modelled as an explicit release step.
